### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | AI use is permitted but must be disclosed. ACES Online journal-update page states Wiley's Research Exchange platform runs a mandatory pre-check before manuscripts reach the CE&S editorial office, screening for plagiarism and possible AI use; authors must disclose any AI use "in accordance with journal and APA expectations, including safeguards taken." This is journal-specific confirmation layered on Wiley's general (publisher-wide, not CE&S-specific) generative-AI authorship policy, which bans listing AI as an author and requires disclosure of substantive generative-AI use with tool name/version and purpose (source: Wiley Generative AI Policy PDF, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/pb-assets/assets/15405885/Generative%20AI%20Policy_September%202023-1695231878293.pdf). No CE&S-specific numeric threshold or outright ban found, hence leniency scored mid-range (conditional/disclosure-based, not open, not banned). |
| **Source URL** | https://acesonline.net/counselor-education-and-supervision-journal-update/ |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Empirical (quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods) and conceptual/policy-practice articles on counselor education, clinical supervision, and professional issues in counseling training programs. Recent 2025-2026 published titles confirm active topics: AI integration in counselor education/supervision (concept-mapping study, Vol 65 Iss 1, 2026), empirically-based supervision models (Vol 64, 2025), doctoral-student diversity/equity experiences (Black men in doctoral CE programs, 2026), internship experiences with older-adult populations (2026), and group-work supervision with school-counseling site supervisors (2026).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** quantitative/empirical research, qualitative research, mixed-methods research, conceptual/theoretical pieces, policy and practice articles, brief reports, innovative pedagogical methods articles
